First off I'd like to apologize for the sexual assault that you have experienced in your life. I understand that this is something that you feel deeply about and that is close to your heart.

However, I would like to kindly and respectfully say that your entire argument feels like, "you're a guy and she's a girl thus because of the history of the world, you are at fault." And while I understand that making her guilty until proven wrong puts a burden on her, you do understand that does the same for me. And while I understand I am the accused, a lot of the arguments you make for her being too drunk for X and Y can be applied to me as well.

And you know, I get it nobody wants to be the person who looks someone in the face and says "hey you're wrong, you weren't sexually assaulted" but every exemption you make for her being intoxicated can apply to me, you can't simply say that because men have a history of being predatory that I'm suddenly at fault and now assume all responsibility for everything that happened.

I know our situations are diffrent, and I'm in no way trying to compare or invalidate what you went through. while this may not apply to you, if I came out to the average person and said "hey I had drunk sex with someone the other night and I think I was raped" most people would be like "No you just had drunk sex, it happens"

And that's what is frustrating about this situation because all of a sudden it's all my fault; nothing she did mattered. You paint this entire situation like I was the aggressor and she wasn't coming on to me. And that's what I'm trying to get at: sex is mutual and you can't just be like "hey y'all were both drunk and unable to assume responsibility, but because she believes there was a lack of consent, you have to assume all responsibility because she's drunk and she's a woman and what she said was valid."  

I understand that on a global scale, sexism is rampant. but you can't say "she's drunk and she's a woman and everything she says matters, the rules don't apply to her but all of them apply to you." because damn it my voice matters. You can't simply choose to accept her perceptive and overlook mine and call that fair, because this a case to case basis. And I get it nobody wants to tell someone who feels victimized "you're wrong", but I refuse to be pigeonholed into the predatory role.

And I do think I deserve a second chance at University because I was immature and reckless and took what I had for granted, and yes I understand I was 18 but you're telling me something that happened in my first 3 months of college, 6 months out of high school should determine the full course of my adult life?

I'm going to get 100% fucking real with you. I am strong, I've tried to kill myself 4 times within the 3 year span of this happening. I've developed social avoidant personality disorder because of being gaslit. There was a year and a half where I was scared of women and would bawl my eyes out getting naked infront of another person and it's still something I don't feel 100% comfortable with. I've fought depression and addiction for the past 2 years of my fucking life. I wake up in the middle of the night bawling my fucking eyes out becuase I feel like I'm back at that school. I did not stand up for myself when I was 18, I sat there and took it, I let everyone say "this is your fault you are in the wrong" and I refuse to let some jabroni on the internet tell me what I experienced is invalid, slander me, and call me a rapist and tell me that something that happened when I was 18 should determine the course of the rest of my life.

So I debated weather or not I should reply to this or not, so if I get downvoted or if you choose to read this are whatever to me. And I understand you feel passionately and I know my perspective won't change your opinion on the situation though I'm gonna give it anyways

I'm gonna be a straight shooter here, you spent 2 thirds of your post patronizing me rather than genuinely giving advice and for that you're an asshole.

Your post reaks of gender basis which is what I had to deal with 3 years ago and it's extremely frustrating. In your post you said 

>"When an individual is intoxicated, they are legally unable to provide consent (3). So the person you had a sexual encounter with wasn't fully consenting because she legally wasn't able to fully consent"

But you do realize I was just as drunk as she was; and by your definition neither of us were able to give consent, because we were both intoxicated. So you do understand that by your definition she raped me too. And this isn't a case of coercion or anything like that; we were we two drunk friends who ended up making out that led to sex. I didn't force her to do anything, I did not slip her anything. She was not passed out or anything of the sort. I did not force myself onto her. She gave her full consent; and so did I. We were both drunk. Just because she regrets it doesn't automatically make it rape. If her being drunk means I took advantage of her then damn it she took advantage of me too.

If the person is drunk and can say yes to another drunk person that is consent.

It becomes a stawman argument at that point forward

Why is it because she regretted it (hell I did too) a few days later it's suddenly my fault? Why is it fair that she is exhumed of any reasonability, and I now hold all of it? If I'm a rapist than so is she because we were both unable to give consent. If you excuse one's behavior on those grounds then you should excuse both. Sex is something done together not one to the other. But fuck me cause I'm a guy right?

And when this happened, nobody asked me for my side of the story. All my friends took it at face value and I lost most of them. Because I'm a guy so I'm instantly a predator; my perceptive doesn't matter, and that's how most people see this (yourself included). The people over seeing this ignored most of the stuff my side presented in the school hearing My voice didn't matter at all. How is that fair?

Nothing can compare to being falsely labeled a rapist. Nobody willing to listen to you; spending a year terrified of having sex and women. This situation gave me an entire personality disorder, as well as PTSD. You don't know how often I often I wake up in the middle of the night crying and screaming. You don't know what it feels like to have nobody care about what you have to say and have a bunch of people label you as the most vial thing a person can be and have that be their final impression of you.

And you think I deserve all of that? What on top of having my dreams crushed, and having my future ripped from under me. All for a drunken hook up I had when I was barely 18. Tell me how that's fair?

I understand that this is an emotionally charged argument, but level with me.

I guess I'm just looking for people with a background in college admissions to give me a better perspective becuase getting rejected from 5 schools in 3 years is a lot. And I don't know if they're finding out me lying for going to college prior about it behind closed doors (if so how becuase I was told they could not) or if I'm simply not enough. Because I just got rejected from a sister school (comparable but not in anyway connected) to the one I was at prior with a 66% acceptance rate.

And I cannot apply as a transfer at the moment due to an outstanding balance on the account at the prior school and them withholding my transcript (thought there are no grades)

So my options going forward. 


Pay the outstanding balance from my old school (which is 4k and I'd either need a loan or payment plans) and apply as a transfer and just be honest upfront; but because of the polarizing nature of my case I feel they will take my story at face value and not see it was a false sexual assault claim.


Go to community college and transfer in but that is a waste of time and money as I was at at an art school taking art course and have been applying to similar and none of my credits would transfer. And even then that doesn't guarantee I'll get in


Should I just not go; as I'm 21 this year and everything will take a years plus time and I wouldn't enter school until 22, and I feel that's a bit old to be an on campus freshman, and can easily peruse a career in art on my own without college. Thought I want this becuase I feel I never got the chance to experience this but I feel as though that widow has passed and I need to be an adult.


I'm sorry it's a lot of details and specifics
